thread:
Anya: Noticed canary enrollment not sticking. Sent X-Canary header, first req hit canary, next 3 from same client went back to stable.
Mike: I can reproduce locally. Router logs show 'allocated: canary' then 'sticky assigned: stable' within 10s.
Leena: Pulling traces. Eval order in code is: check_sticky -> compute_hash -> run_guards -> finalize. So sticky path prevents guard-based enrollment.
Josh: Is the design to have explicit guards (headers/cookies) override existing sticky assignments? I thought explicit opt-ins should take precedence.
Anya: Yes, user expectation: if client explicitly signals X-Canary:true, we should honor that and persist it.
Mike: Additional oddity: when guard tries to route to canary but health check disallows it, we record stable in sticky store. Later when canary recovers, hash-based allocation flips some users -> creates oscillation.
Leena: I filed RB-4567 for guard ordering + sticky recording race.
Josh: Proposed quick fix: evaluate guards before sticky check. If a guard chooses a route, set sticky to that route (if sticky_enabled). Otherwise fall through to sticky/hash selection.
Leena: Will open PR with changes + unit tests for health-fallback behavior. Also adding explicit 'guard precedence' flag in router config for safety.
Anya: Pausing rollout until patch lands.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused by @Anya at 2026-03-18T12:14:22Z
Mike: Also logging UX idea: surface 'guard precedence' and 'sticky recording' behavior in console with a short note in rollout details.
Leena: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/router/pulls/789. Tests added.
Anya: Thx everyone. Patch review now; will coordinate hotfix release once approved.
